trans-unit.source: The Field Journal: Learning That Stays

Back at their desk, students expand their notes with extended analysis, personal reflection, and connections to what they already know. Teachers can review, respond, and promote entries to the student's permanent portfolio.

trans-unit.source: From a White Paper to a Working Platform: Peripateticware 2007–2026

The paper was written at a moment when 3G hadn't fully rolled out, the iPhone was months away from launch, and "app" wasn't yet a common word. Its predictions — that cell phones would become 1-for-1 classroom devices, that mobile networks would reach remote regions, that GPS would become cheap enough to put in every student's pocket — all came true. The products the paper called for did not.

trans-unit.source: That's where Peri comes in. Peri is Peripateticware's AI guide — named, like the software, after the Aristotelian method. Peri doesn't answer questions. It asks them. It follows the five-phase inquiry sequence — Engage, Observe, Analyse, Explain, Apply — that Aristotle used in the Lyceum and that cognitive science has since validated as a path to genuine understanding, not just retention.
